traps: Claiming AD is perpendicular to BC instead of being an angle bisector.
Stating that AP is a median of BC without showing it bisects the angles at Z.
Confusing the base angles of the isosceles triangles (e.g., swapping ∠ABC with ∠BCA).
Assuming triangles ABC and DBC are congruent rather than merely isosceles.
Giving only one of the required angle equalities (e.g., only ∠AAB = ∠AAC) and omitting the others.

checks.ask: Does the answer note that triangles ABC and DBC are isosceles (AB = AC and DB = DC)?
Does the answer use the base‑angles theorem to state that ∠ABC = ∠BCA and ∠DBC = ∠BCD?
Does the answer show that ∠AAB = ∠AAC (i.e., AD bisects ∠BAC)?
Does the answer state that AP bisects both ∠Z A and ∠Z D (i.e., ∠ZAP = ∠PAZ and ∠ZDP = ∠PDZ)?
